newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks roar to 6th straight record close.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks roar to 6th straight record close.

text.p: Mexican stocks shed some of their earlier gains but still left even the recent slew of impressive gains far behind to notch up their sixth record close in a row Tuesday.
Dealers said foreign and domestic investors crowded a market basking in euphoria in the wake of smoother-than-expected midterm elections Sunday, amid a strong tailwind blowing from Wall Street.
Final closing prices showed the blue-chip IPC share index had soared 79.90 points, or 1.69 percent, to a new record of 4,821.14.
"Basically, what we are seeing is that players who stayed on the sidelines last week are rushing in on the benefits of great elections," a desk trader said.

"Investors are overweighting Mexico in their portfolios, and there has been a slew of country recommendations favouring Mexico, cutting Chile and Brazil," he added. "Furthermore, forecasts have been upgraded for key indicators."

A Salomon Brothers report released Tuesday said the brokerage was "shifting weight to Mexico from Chile," as short-term risk in Mexico had been reduced by "the perceived integrity of the July 6 elections."
Caspian Research issued a report raising their year-end target for the IPC to 5,500 points from 4,700, based on "clean, transparent and peaceful" elections.

Mexico held elections Sunday for the lower house of Congress, one-quarter of the Senate, several state governors and for the first time in modern history, Mexico City mayor. The presidency was not up for election.

Analysts noted the elections were much freer than in recent years of fraud allegations, and the ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party gracefully accepted preliminary returns showing it had suffered its worst setback since 1929.
Dealers said they had so many buy orders the market needed to impose trading halts and use a screen-trading backup system to handle a record level of more than 8,562 deals settled.
"We were spinning around like firecrackers," one floor trader said.
Trading volume and turnover were very heavy at more than 209 million shares and 3.10 billion pesos ($392 million), respectively.
Dealers said blue chips and American Depository Receipts (ADRs) led the rally.
Telefonos de Mexico (Telmex), which has the heaviest weighting on the IPC, gained 15 centavos (2 cents) to 20.75 pesos ($2.63), a peso record.
The telecommunications company's ADRs advanced 87.5 cents to $52.75, their highest level since the December 1994 peso crisis. The Dow Jones, meanwhile, gained 103.81 to end at a record of 7,962.31.
Bancomer, one of Mexico's biggest financial firms, gained 28 centavos (4 cents) to 4.70 pesos (59 cents).
Dealers said financial stocks in general gained on expectations that forecast cuts in domestic interest rates would ease their past-due loan burdens.
Bancomer and Telmex together accounted for some 23 percent of all shares traded.
Cement maker Cemex climbed 1.40 pesos (18 cents) to 37.90 pesos ($4.80).
On the broad market, gainers far outstripped sliders, by 92 to 26, out of a total of 134 stocks that changed hands.
